tldr: Microsoft’s Agent Framework Python package was published in two malicious versions; check dependency histories and rotate credentials if either version ran in your environment.
Foundry Agent Service is adding production controls including egress restrictions and deployment to your own AKS clusters, affecting how you design agent network boundaries.
Azure’s new VM zone-resilience preview could simplify recovery of eligible zonal VMs without rebuilding their resources and configuration.

top.title: Foundry hosted agents add egress controls and customer AKS deployment
top.summary: Foundry Agent Service is adding shared subnet IPs, private CA trust, network egress controls, resilient execution and memory snapshots; agents can also be deployed to customer AKS clusters.
top.why: Reassess whether hosted agents now meet your network-isolation requirements or whether you need to run them in your own AKS boundary.

top.title: Azure previews recovery of zonal VMs in another availability zone
top.summary: The preview lets you recover eligible zonal VMs in another zone in the same region while retaining the VM resource and configuration; it uses zone-replicated managed disks.
top.why: Evaluate this as a potential recovery path for zonal workloads, but confirm eligibility and preview limitations before changing your resilience design.

top.title: Azure previews AMD Venice DHasv8 and EHasv8 VM families
top.summary: New DHasv8, DHalsv8 and EHasv8 VMs based on 6th-generation AMD EPYC processors are in preview, with expanded compute and memory configurations and improved storage and networking performance.
top.why: Benchmark these against your current CPU-hosted workloads before choosing VM sizes; the announcement gives no pricing or performance figures yet.

top.title: Guest RDMA on Azure Boost enters public preview
top.summary: Available in all regions, Guest RDMA exposes RDMA directly to guest VMs through the front-end NIC, bypassing the guest networking stack on RDMA data paths to reduce host CPU use and latency.
top.why: Consider testing it for distributed AI or other low-latency workloads where network overhead is a bottleneck, while checking supported VM and application requirements.

top.title: Azure Compute Gallery soft delete is generally available
top.summary: Deleted Azure Compute Gallery image versions can now be recovered during a configurable retention period of 7 to 365 days, and remain deployable while soft-deleted.
top.why: Set a retention period that balances accidental-deletion recovery against keeping obsolete images available for deployment.

also.title: Azure DDoS Protection previews telemetry for normal traffic
also.summary: The preview adds DDoS traffic metrics during normal operation, so teams can establish baselines, set alerts and test monitoring before an attack.

also.title: Azure Backup adds cross-subscription protection for VMs
also.summary: Azure Backup now lets you protect VMs with a Recovery Services vault in another subscription in the same tenant.

also.title: Functions Flex Consumption previews OS dependencies in Linux containers
also.summary: The preview lets Flex Consumption functions package Linux OS-level dependencies, such as Chromium or GnuPG, in a container.

also.title: Azure Front Door Premium previews an AI bot ruleset for WAF
also.summary: The preview adds a Web Application Firewall ruleset for controlling AI crawlers and agents, beyond the limited controls provided by robots.txt.

also.title: Azure SRE Agent previews native AWS and Google Cloud support
also.summary: The agent can investigate incidents across Azure, AWS and Google Cloud, following diagnostic clues such as an Azure app’s dependency on DynamoDB.

also.title: PostgreSQL 19 enters preview on Azure in East Asia
also.summary: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server now supports provisioning PostgreSQL 19 preview servers in the East Asia region.

top.title: Malicious versions of Microsoft Agent Framework package stole credentials
top.summary: Attackers published malicious versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft’s Agent Framework Python package to PyPI, using Microsoft’s publisher account; the versions were designed to steal cloud and developer credentials.
top.why: Check dependency lockfiles, build logs and developer environments for those versions, and rotate exposed credentials if they were installed or executed.

top.title: Power, cooling and network capacity are constraining AI deployments
top.summary: Reports from SC26 say enterprises are finding that power, cooling and network throughput—not just GPU availability—can determine whether AI data-center and edge-inference deployments can run effectively.
top.why: Include facility power, thermal capacity and network throughput in AI capacity planning rather than treating GPU supply as the sole deployment constraint.

also.title: Gemini’s Mac app can now operate across local apps and files
also.summary: Google added computer-use capabilities to its macOS Gemini app for multi-step tasks across desktop apps, local files and the web.

also.title: Signal blocks mobile OS AI agents from reading its screen
also.summary: Signal is restricting screenshots on Android and iOS to prevent built-in AI agents from reading messages and other on-screen data.

also.title: Resolve AI launches SRE-1 for production incident diagnosis
also.summary: Resolve AI introduced SRE-1, a model intended to find root causes of production alerts, alongside a service that puts its agents on call.

top.title: Google donates Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF
top.summary: Google is placing Agent Substrate and gVisor, components of its AI agent infrastructure, under Cloud Native Computing Foundation open-source governance.
top.why: Track whether the projects gain broad adoption: vendor-neutral governance could make them candidates for agent isolation and runtime designs beyond Google’s own stack.

top.title: AWS releases a free local emulator for more than 200 services
top.summary: AWS Emulator is a free, CC0-licensed local stand-in for more than 200 AWS services, generated and maintained by agents; it publishes fidelity scores but does not evaluate IAM.
top.why: It may help test agent-written code locally, but do not treat it as a security or IAM test environment, and account for its unreviewed, agent-generated implementation.

also.title: Apache Iceberg V4 proposes more scalable table metadata
also.summary: The proposed V4 table-format specification redesigns metadata to improve scalability and support more frequent writes, with additional data-management and schema-evolution features.

also.title: Vercel launches a shared message board for coding agents
also.summary: Vercel’s new board gives agents such as Claude Code and Codex a shared place to communicate and divide work.
